item.title: The DNA Breakthrough That Exposed David Fuller’s Double Life
item.description: DNA linked hospital electrician David Fuller to the 1987 murders of Wendy Knell and Caroline Pierce in Kent. A search then uncovered evidence of abuse in hospital mortuaries. He pleaded guilty to both murders and received a whole-life sentence in 2021.

item.title: A Missing License Plate Led Police To Joel Rifkin
item.description: In June 1993, Joel Rifkin fled New York troopers who spotted his missing license plate. After he crashed, police found Tiffany Bresciani’s body in his truck. He confessed to killing 17 women and was ultimately convicted of nine murders, receiving 203 years in prison.

item.title: Joe Arridy’s Pardon Came 72 Years After His Execution
item.description: Colorado executed Joe Arridy, a 23-year-old man with an intellectual disability, in 1939. In 2011, Governor Bill Ritter granted a posthumous pardon, citing overwhelming evidence of innocence, including false and coerced confessions and another man’s admission of guilt.

item.title: Anni Dewani’s Taxi Driver Admitted Helping Kill Her
item.description: Anni Dewani, 28, was killed during her honeymoon in Cape Town in 2010. Her taxi driver pleaded guilty to involvement in a staged hijacking, and two other men were convicted. Her husband, Shrien, was acquitted in 2014 after the judge found the prosecution’s evidence unreliable.

item.title: Tiffany Cole Impersonated Her Victim On A Police Call
item.description: After Reggie and Carol Sumner were kidnapped and killed in 2005, Tiffany Cole posed as Carol during a call with a detective. Phone records and rental-car GPS helped connect the group to the crime. Convicted of both murders, Cole was resentenced to life in prison in 2023

item.title: Jimmy Prout’s Abusers Accompanied Him To Medical Visits
item.description: Jimmy Prout was murdered in North Shields in 2016 after prolonged abuse. A review found professionals missed warning signs and never spoke to him alone during the period examined. Zahid Zaman and Ann Corbett were convicted of his murder and jailed for life in 2017.

item.title: Amy Bishop’s Arrest Led Back To Her Brother’s Death
item.description: After professor Amy Bishop killed three colleagues in Alabama in 2010, investigators reopened her brother’s 1986 shooting death, initially ruled accidental. She pleaded guilty to the campus shootings and received life without parole in 2012. The separate murder charge over her brother’s death was withdrawn.

item.title: Cameron Hooker Invented A Secret Group To Prevent Escape
item.description: Abducted in California in 1977, Colleen Stan endured seven years of captivity while Cameron Hooker threatened her with a fictitious organization called “The Company.” His wife eventually exposed the lie, helping Stan leave. Hooker was convicted in 1985 and sentenced to 104 years.
